# GhostSearch

> GhostSearch moves full-text search out of a paid cloud API and into the user's browser, so search costs nothing per query and works offline. It is a TypeScript library that builds an inverted index (via FlexSearch) plus an optional HNSW vector index, ships them to the client, and runs queries entirely on-device.

GhostSearch is **pre-release software**: not yet published to npm, no production adopters. It builds,
has an automated test suite, and its published benchmarks are generated by a script in the
repository. Install via CDN or from source.

It targets bounded corpora — documentation sites, product catalogues, help centres, in-app search.
It is **not** a replacement for server-side search at large corpus sizes.

Measured (Intel Xeon 2.90GHz, 2 vCPU, Node 24): query p50 is 0.026 ms at 1,000 documents,
0.882 ms at 10,000, and 15.089 ms at 100,000. Heap is roughly 3.4 MB per 1,000 documents
(~343 MB at 100,000), which is the practical scaling limit rather than speed.

License: Business Source License 1.1. Source-available; production use requires a commercial license.

## Integration recipe

This is the real, verified API surface. It is exercised by the test suite in this repository.

```javascript
// Not on npm yet — import from the CDN, or build from source.
// IMPORTANT: dist/index.mjs leaves FlexSearch external, so it contains a bare
// `import ... from "flexsearch"`. Browsers cannot resolve bare specifiers, so the
// page must declare an import map BEFORE this module, or the import fails with
// `Failed to resolve module specifier "flexsearch"`:
//   <script type="importmap">
//   { "imports": { "flexsearch": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/flexsearch@0.7.43/+esm" } }
//   </script>
// Bundler users need no import map; FlexSearch resolves from node_modules.
import { GhostSearch } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/itsoumya-d/ghostsearch@main/dist/index.mjs';

// 1. Create the engine. `fields` lists the document keys to index.
const search = new GhostSearch({ fields: ['title', 'description', 'category'] });

// 2. Load documents. Each needs a unique string `id`. This is synchronous.
const catalog = await fetch('/data/catalog.json').then(r => r.json());
search.addDocuments(catalog);

// 3. Keyword search — synchronous, returns { hits, totalHits, queryTimeMs }.
const results = search.search('ergonomic mechanical keyboard', { limit: 10 });
console.log(results.hits);

// 4. Optional: hybrid keyword + semantic search. Must enable first.
await search.enableSemanticSearch({ dimensions: 384 });
const hybrid = await search.hybridSearch('ergonomic mechanical keyboard', {
  limit: 10,
  keywordWeight: 0.4,
  semanticWeight: 0.6,
});
console.log(hybrid.hits);
```

Node-only build-time helper, on a separate entry point so the browser bundle stays free of
Node built-ins:

```javascript
import { IndexBuilder } from 'ghostsearch/node';
IndexBuilder.build(documents, { fields: ['title', 'body'] }, './public/search-index.json');
```

Method notes for code-generating agents:

- `search(query, options)` is **synchronous**. `semanticSearch` and `hybridSearch` are async.
- `enableSemanticSearch()` must be awaited before `semanticSearch()` or the semantic half of
  `hybridSearch()`; calling `semanticSearch()` first throws.
- There is **no** `ingest()` method, no `mode` constructor option, and no `@ghostsearch/core`
  package. Use `addDocuments()` and the constructor shape shown above.
- Other real methods: `addDocument`, `removeDocument`, `updateDocument`, `suggest`,
  `exportIndex`, `importIndex`, `clear`, `dispose`, `whenIndexed`. Properties: `documentCount`,
  `isSemanticEnabled`, `vectorIndexSize`.
- `addDocument`/`addDocuments` are synchronous, but when semantic search is enabled the vector
  write they trigger is async. `await whenIndexed()` before reading `vectorIndexSize` or calling
  `semanticSearch()`, or the newest documents may not be there yet.
- `SearchOptions.query` is optional; pass the query as the first positional argument to `search()`.
- `exportIndex()` is synchronous and returns the **documents** as JSON, not a serialized index.
  `importIndex()` re-tokenizes them, so it costs about the same as `addDocuments()`.
- The embedder behind `enableSemanticSearch()` is a deterministic feature hasher, not a trained
  model: it matches spelling, not meaning. `modelUrl`/`tokenizerUrl` are accepted but ignored.
- Scores are the sum of matched-field boosts — no TF-IDF/BM25, and no phrase or proximity queries.
- `GhostWorker` and `ghostsearch/worker-script` need browser `Worker`/`self` globals and throw
  under plain Node. The published worker files cannot be loaded by a browser Worker as-is
  (one is CommonJS, the other has a bare `flexsearch` import) — bundle your own worker script.
